ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations (sourcemax/by_inst), maximum over binary packages of the source package
selection: Four control-verified C++ JSON paths rank by recorded Debian source-package sourcemax installations: JsonCpp 32,707, simdjson 2,688, nlohmann/json 1,799, RapidJSON 899. Boost.JSON 1.92.0 is control-verified but primary-unranked: its Debian source boost1.83 covers all of Boost, so it carries only the separately labeled libboost-json-dev fallback of 1,749 installs. The source metric favors runtime packages; development-package counts are a separately labeled cross-check.
uncertainty: Five independent C++ JSON parser families pass two valid controls and scoped parser source/AFL feedback. RapidJSON 1.1.0 is a 2016 release that needs Clang -fdelayed-template-parsing to build without source changes on this toolchain; this target uses AddressSanitizer and AFL++, without UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. Source-package installations favor runtime packages and undercount header-only libraries; RapidJSON is header-only with 899 Debian development-package installs. Boost.JSON has no JSON-specific Debian source count, so it has no primary rank; its libboost-json-dev fallback (1,749) is not comparable to sourcemax values. Five documentation leads remain unverified. The search records 320 Debian source-name hits; no complete top-ten claim follows. JSON-specific use is unknown; valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.
